title: Soda Bread
subtitle: A quick, no-yeast Irish loaf ready in under an hour
excerpt: Soda bread uses bicarbonate of soda instead of yeast, so there is no proving time. Mix, shape, bake and it is ready.
sourceNotes: Soda bread became a staple of Irish cooking in the 1840s when bicarbonate of soda became widely available. It replaced yeast-leavened breads in many households as it required no proving time and no specialist equipment.

recipe.freezeNotes: Slice before freezing. Toast from frozen.

content.text: Do not overwork the dough. Mix just until it comes together, then shape it quickly and get it straight into the oven.
Preheat your oven to 200C. Lightly flour a baking tray.
Put the flour in a large bowl. Add 1 teaspoon of salt and 1 teaspoon of bicarbonate of soda.
Make a well in the centre. Pour in the milk.
Mix quickly with a fork or your hand until the dough just comes together. It will be shaggy.
Tip out onto the floured tray. Shape into a round about 4cm thick.
Cut a deep cross across the top with a sharp knife.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped on the bottom.
Cool on a wire rack for at least 10 minutes before slicing.

items.cause: Dough was overworked or bicarbonate of soda is stale.
items.fix: Mix minimally and check the bicarbonate of soda is fresh.

items.symptom: Crust is hard but centre is doughy.
items.cause: Oven was too hot or loaf was too thick.
items.fix: Reduce the oven by 10C and flatten the loaf slightly next time.
Check the self-raising flour has not expired.
